[ASSISTANT_SAID] To minimize compatibility issues when assembling a PC for VR gaming, the assistant provided the following tips:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Check the recommended system requirements of the VR headset.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Choose a motherboard that supports the latest processors and graphics cards.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Choose a processor and graphics card combination that meets or exceeds the VR headset's requirements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Ensure the power supply unit (PSU) can provide sufficient power.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Ensure components are compatible and supported by the operating system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Check that the case has enough space for components and airflow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Install the latest drivers for all components.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Regularly check for software and firmware updates.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Memory: 16 GB or more of DDR4 RAM with high clock speeds and low latency.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Power Supply Unit: EVGA SuperNOVA 750W or Corsair RM750X.
